chunks.text: 80-year-old male, Retired, resident of Ang Mo Kio, Singapore.
General Anesthesia with Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA)

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Lim, the anesthesiologist who will be taking care of you during your hernia repair surgery. I'd like to go through some questions to make sure we're all set for tomorrow's procedure. Is that okay with you?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, sure, Doctor. I'm ready.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Let's start with your medical history. You've been diagnosed with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, benign prostatic hyperplasia, and osteoarthritis in your knees. Can you tell me a bit about how these are being managed?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure. My blood pressure is under control with losartan. I take metformin for my diabetes, and tamsulosin for my prostate. For my knees, I take diclofenac when the pain gets bad, like after walking too much.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you. Now, regarding your medications, I see in your records that you were on aspirin 75 mg daily. Can you confirm if you're still taking that, and if not, when did you stop and why?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, I stopped taking aspirin already. It's been about two years ago. I had some stomach discomfort, like heartburn, so I stopped. I didn't have any issues since then, so I just continued with the other medications.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: I see. That's important to know. Are you currently taking all your regular medications as prescribed, except for the aspirin?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, Doctor. I take losartan every morning, metformin twice a day, and tamsulosin once at night. Diclofenac only when needed.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Do you have any known allergies to medications or other substances?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, none that I know of.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia? If so, were there any complications?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I had a minor operation on my finger many years ago, and that was under general anesthesia. I don't remember any problems, just a bit of nausea after.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks for sharing that. How about your current physical condition? Are you able to walk independently, climb stairs, and perform daily activities without much difficulty?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I can walk and climb stairs, but sometimes my knees give me trouble if I overdo it. Otherwise, I'm quite independent.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Finally, have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, Doctor. I stopped eating after 8 PM last night, as instructed. Just a bit of water with my morning medications.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Well, Mr. Tan, that covers most of what I needed to know. We'll be using general anesthesia with a laryngeal mask airway for your surgery. I'll make sure to note your medication changes and allergies in your chart. If you have any more questions, feel free to ask.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Thank you, Doctor. I think that's all from me for now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] LMA 40 size inserted, no difficulty

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] IV line established, two liters of normal saline running

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] increase sevoflurane to two percent due to increased blood pressure

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20]  administer one thousand milligrams of paracetamol IV for pain management

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:40] decrease sevoflurane to one point five percent as blood pressure stabilized

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Tan. How are you feeling after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm okay, doctor. A bit tired, but not too bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's good to hear. Can you tell me your pain level out of 10? Any discomfort at the incision site or elsewhere?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe a 4 or 5, mostly at the hernia site. It's manageable, I think.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright. Have you felt any nausea or dizziness since waking up? Any issues with vomiting?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, no nausea. I feel fine that way. Just a bit thirsty, actually.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. How about your breathing? Any shortness of breath or discomfort from the LMA during the procedure?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I don't remember much, but I didn't wake up choking or anything. My throat feels a bit sore, but it's mild.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's expected sometimes with the LMA. We'll monitor that. Any recollection of the surgery itself?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, nothing at all. I was out completely, which is good.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Since you have a history of hypertension and diabetes, we'll keep an eye on your vitals and sugar levels. Any chest pain, dizziness, or urinary difficulty from BPH?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No chest pain, and I went to the toilet before surgery, so I think I'm okay for now. My knees are aching a bit, but that's usual.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. We'll keep you comfortable and monitor everything. Let the nurse know if anything changes, okay?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Will do, doctor. Thanks for checking on me.

80-year-old male undergoing elective inguinal hernia repair under general anesthesia with LMA.

Patient has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, benign prostatic hyperplasia, and osteoarthritis in knees. Current medications include losartan, metformin, tamsulosin, and as-needed diclofenac for knee pain. No known drug allergies.

Intra-operative course included propofol induction, LMA placement, fluid administration, and sevoflurane for anesthesia. Paracetamol was given for pain. Blood pressure fluctuations were managed with sevoflurane adjustments.

Anticipated issues include risk of post-operative nausea and vomiting (PONV), potential airway complications due to LMA use in a patient with BPH, need for glycemic control monitoring, risk of hypotension or hypertension due to anesthetic and antihypertensive interactions, pain management challenges, and monitoring for fluid overload.

Monitor for signs of PONV, maintain vigilance for airway complications, ensure glycemic control, closely monitor blood pressure, assess pain and adjust management as needed, and watch for signs of fluid overload.
Patient reports pain level of 4 or 5 at the hernia site, which is manageable.
Patient denies any nausea or vomiting since waking up from surgery.
Patient reports mild throat soreness, which is expected after LMA use.
Patient has no recollection of the surgery, indicating effective general anesthesia.
Patient denies chest pain, dizziness, or urinary difficulty, but mentions usual knee aching.
Patient was maintained on current medications: Losartan, Metformin, Tamsulosin, and had Aspirin discontinued 2 years ago due to stomach discomfort.
General Anesthesia with Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA) was used for the elective inguinal hernia repair.
Patient's vitals and sugar levels will be monitored due to history of hypertension and diabetes.
